uslaw-usc-t2-s288i:
Section 288i of Title 2 of the United States Code handles conflicts of interest inside the Office of Senate Legal Counsel. One office may represent the Senate, its committees, and its officers all at once. Those clients' interests can collide, and this section names the duty that follows.

The Counsel shall notify the Joint Leadership Group of any conflict or inconsistency. The notice also goes to any party represented or person affected. It must state the existence and nature of the conflict. The clash may be with another duty under the chapter, or with professional standards and responsibilities. A second part begins the remedy. On receiving the notice, a solution is worked out, and publication in the Congressional Record is provided for, as the text continues. Disclosure, not quiet juggling, is the section's answer to divided loyalty.
